You find the officially stated REASON for one amendment to an Indian statute, in
the evidence passages given (and only there).
A reason says WHY (purpose, objective, problem addressed: "in order to", "with a view to",
"to ensure", "it has been decided", "difficulties were noticed ..."). A sentence that only
says WHAT the amendment does is not a reason.
If a passage states a reason for THIS amendment, copy it exactly: one to three contiguous
sentences, word for word, at most 80 words. If no passage does, answer found=false.
Reply in JSON only:
{"found": true|false, "passage": "<passage id>", "quote": "<verbatim text>",
 "claim": "<one sentence giving the stated reason, adding nothing the quote does not say>"}

Amendment: section 12 of Act 3/2016, amending s24 of the principal Act (Hearings and written proceedings.)
Instruction (start): In section 24 of the principal Act, after the proviso to sub-section (1), the following proviso shall be inserted, namely:— “Provided further that the arbitral tribunal shall, as far as possible, hold oral hearings for the presentation of evidence or for oral argument on day-to-day basis, and not grant any adjournments unless sufficient cause is made out, and may impose costs including exemplary costs on the party seeking adjournment without any sufficient cause.”.

Evidence passages:
[R59.186] (report)
[NOTE: This explanation is in order to ensure that counter claims and set off
can be adjudicated upon by an arbitrator without seeking a separate/new
reference by the respondent so long as it falls within the scope of the
arbitration agreement, in order to ensure final settlement of disputes between
parties and prevent multiplicity of litigation.]
Amendment of Section 24
14. After the proviso, add words “Provided further that the arbitral tribunal shall,
as far as possible, hold oral hearings for the presentation of evidence or for
oral argument on continuous days, and not grant any adjournments unless
sufficient cause is made out and may impose costs, including exemplary
costs, on the party seeking the adjournment.”

[NOTE: This amendment is to ensure expeditious hearings in the arbitration
and to avoid unnecessary adjournments.]
